decisions.quote: Our replication of Model 2 in Table 3  yields a coefficient of  b = -.47 (SE = .07, p < .001) on  the “Proportion natives” variable (see Table 1 in the attached Appendix).  Thus, this reproduction of the claim was successful according to the SCORE criteria.
decisions.reason: The original study reported b = -.51 (SE = .06, p < .001) for Table 3, Model 2, whereas re-running the baseline model produced b = -.47 (SE = .07, p < .001) (and b = -.483, SE = .072 under the original code's network inclusion criteria). The authors also identified discrepancies between the original code and paper as well as a loop misassignment error in the original code that double-counted results. Because the analysis ran and produced comparable numbers that differed from the original reported numbers beyond rounding, the codebook value for outcome_computation is 'computational issues' rather than 'computationally reproducible' (which was based on the substantive SCORE directional/significance criterion).

decisions.quote: Overall, across all of our models, we find a negative, statistically significant (p < .01) coefficient on “Proportion natives” that is similar in size to the coefficient reported in the original study.
decisions.reason: Contrary to the shipped value 'not checked', the authors explicitly conducted multiple robustness checks varying ERGM convergence thresholds, visual inspection of MCMC trace/density plots, network inclusion criteria (paper vs. code specifications), and missing-data handling across six models in Appendix Tables 1 and 2, concluding that the negative, statistically significant effect held across all specifications.
